'''Troy A. Van Voorhis''' (born 1976) is an American [[chemist]]. He is currently the Haslam and Dewey Professor of Chemistry at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="MIT">{{Cite web |url=http://chemistry.mit.edu/people/van-voorhis-troy |title=Troy Van Voorhis |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=April 30, 2017}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Troy Van Voorhis graduated from [[North Central High School (Indianapolis)|North Central High School]], Indianapolis, Indiana, in 1994. He graduated with a B.A. from [[Rice University]] in 1997.<ref name="MIT" /> 
While at [[Rice University|Rice]], Van Voorhis conducted research under [[Gustavo Scuseria|Gus Scuseria]], notably developing the first practical{{citation needed|date=April 2022}} implementation of a Meta-GGA in [[density functional theory]] (DFT).<ref>{{Cite journal |title=A novel form for the exchange-correlation energy functional |year=1998 |publisher=American Institute of Physics |doi=10.1063/1.476577 |last1=Van Voorhis |first1=Troy |last2=Scuseria |first2=Gustavo E. |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |volume=109 |issue=2 |pages=400–410 |bibcode=1998JChPh.109..400V }}</ref> He went on to pursue a Ph.D. in [[theoretical chemistry]] under [[Martin Head-Gordon]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], graduating in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chemistry.mit.edu/people/van-voorhis-troy |title=Troy Van Voorhis |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=November 14, 2017}}</ref> He went on to [[Harvard University]] for postdoctoral research with [[Eric J. Heller]] and [[David R. Reichman]]. In 2003, he joined the department of chemistry at [[MIT]] as a faculty member and was promoted to full professor in 2012. Since 2019, he has been the head of the department of chemistry at MIT.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Troy Van Voorhis named head of the Department of Chemistry |url=https://news.mit.edu/2019/troy-van-voorhis-named-head-department-chemistry-1001 |access-date=2022-04-15 |website=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=October 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

Besides scientific research, he has made numerous videos with the [[Veritas Forum]], in which he discusses his belief that science and religion are not in conflict.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=troy+van+voorhis]</ref>
